Demand is structurally constrained by government budgets, regulatory processes, and the fixed number of jurisdictions, so cheaper analysis would not dramatically expand headcount. Since disruption stays at the moderate level (<=6), the occupation is best classified as resilient: AI augments the analytical periphery without reshaping the human-centric core.

title: Veterinarians
rationale: The core work of veterinarians is heavily physical and hands-on—examining animals, performing surgery, dressing wounds, vaccinating, and traveling to farms—which AI cannot replace, though AI does assist with diagnosis, imaging interpretation, and treatment recommendations, placing disruption in the moderate range. Demand elasticity is moderate because cheaper, faster diagnostics could unlock latent demand (more pet owners pursuing advanced care, more underserved livestock coverage), but physical capacity and the need for in-person animal handling cap expansion. Because disruption remains at or below 6, the occupation is resilient: AI augments diagnostic and administrative tasks but does not reshape the fundamentally physical, compassion-driven core of veterinary practice.

title: Veterinary assistants and laboratory animal caretakers
rationale: The core work — feeding, bathing, restraining, cleaning cages, sterilizing instruments, monitoring post-surgery animals, and assisting during procedures — is overwhelmingly physical, hands-on, and requires real-time presence with unpredictable live animals. AI touches only peripheral tasks like scheduling and recordkeeping, leaving the essential duties untouched. Demand could expand moderately as cheaper veterinary throughput unlocks more pet care, but the physical bottleneck of human handling caps elasticity. With disruption far below the threshold, this occupation is clearly resilient to AI.

title: Veterinary technologists and technicians
rationale: The core work is overwhelmingly hands-on physical animal care—restraining, bathing, administering anesthesia, taking x-rays, performing surgery prep, and providing nursing care—which AI cannot perform, so disruption is low. AI touches only peripheral tasks like recording case histories, interpreting lab tests, and informational counseling. Demand for veterinary services is moderately elastic since lower-cost diagnostics and rising pet spending could expand treatment options, but headcount is fundamentally tied to physical presence with animals. Because disruption is well below 7, the occupation is resilient: AI augments record-keeping and diagnostics but does not reshape the manual, in-person core of the job.

title: Waiters and waitresses
rationale: The core work is physical and interpersonal—carrying trays, serving food, reading customers, and providing in-person hospitality—none of which AI can perform; AI touches only peripheral systems like ordering kiosks and point-of-sale technology, which marginally reduce headcount but don't reshape the job. Demand elasticity is low because dining-out volume is constrained by population, disposable income, and the value of human service in restaurants rather than by the cost of order-taking. Because disruption is well under the threshold of 7, this occupation is resilient: automation nibbles at the edges (self-service kiosks, carryout) but the hands-on serving role persists.

title: Water and wastewater treatment plant and system operators
rationale: Disruption is moderate: while monitoring, data recording, and process optimization are increasingly handled by computerized SCADA systems and could be enhanced by AI, the core work requires physical presence to inspect equipment, collect samples, add chemicals, perform maintenance, manually operate during malfunctions, and respond to emergencies in difficult-to-access locations. Elasticity is very low because water treatment demand is fixed by population and infrastructure—cheaper or faster operations do not cause society to consume dramatically more treated water, and regulatory requirements mandate licensed human oversight regardless. Because disruption stays at or below 6, the occupation is resilient: automation trims headcount modestly (as BLS already projects a 7% decline) but AI touches the monitoring periphery rather than reshaping the hands-on, safety-critical core of the job.

title: Water transportation workers
rationale: Core work involves physical operation, maintenance, and crewing of vessels at sea, with hands-on tasks like engine repair, deckhand labor, mooring, and navigating local hazards that require human presence aboard ship; AI assists with navigation, route optimization, and logging but cannot replace the physical and safety-critical crew functions in the next decade, so disruption is low. Demand for water transportation is tied to bulk commodity flows and trade volumes, which are structurally constrained and not suppressed by labor cost or speed, so cheaper operation would not dramatically expand cargo or passenger demand, yielding low elasticity. With disruption well below the threshold, this occupation is resilient — AI touches navigation and monitoring at the periphery while the core seafaring work remains human-dependent.

title: Web developers and digital designers
rationale: Web development and digital design are almost entirely digital cognitive tasks—coding in HTML/JavaScript, designing layouts, building prototypes—all of which are squarely in the path of current AI coding and design tools that already generate functional sites and interfaces. This drives a very high disruption score, as AI can automate large portions of routine front-end and back-end work. However, demand elasticity is high: cheaper, faster web creation unlocks substantial latent demand as more businesses, e-commerce sites, and mobile interfaces get built that previously couldn't justify the cost. Because productivity gains are likely absorbed by expanded output rather than headcount cuts (BLS already projects growth), the occupation fits augment—each worker produces dramatically more while total employment stays stable or grows.

title: Welders, cutters, solderers, and brazers
rationale: The core work is heavily physical and manual—hand-held torch manipulation, precise positioning of molten metal, working in awkward positions and confined spaces, lifting heavy materials—all requiring real-world presence and dexterity that AI cannot perform. AI touches only peripheral tasks like blueprint interpretation or process documentation, while physical welding automation is robotics-based and progresses slowly for non-repetitive, on-site, or custom work. Demand is moderately constrained by infrastructure cycles and manufacturing automation rather than AI cost barriers, so productivity gains would not dramatically expand headcount. Because disruption is very low, the occupation is clearly resilient regardless of elasticity.

title: Wholesale and manufacturing sales representatives
rationale: Much of the work—lead identification, customer outreach, report writing, order processing, and product Q&A—is cognitive and language-based, and AI tools (CRM automation, chatbots, lead scoring, automated outreach) already materially augment these tasks. However, the core of B2B sales rests on relationship-building, trust, negotiation, and in-person presence at trade shows and client sites, which AI cannot replace, keeping disruption moderate. Demand elasticity is low-to-moderate: total sales volume is constrained by actual business purchasing needs rather than the cost of sales contact, so cheaper outreach doesn't proportionally multiply the value of human reps and tends to thin the headcount needed per dollar of sales. Because disruption stays at or below 6 and the human relationship core remains central, the occupation is resilient—AI reshapes peripheral and administrative tasks but does not transform the fundamental work of consultative selling.

title: Wind turbine technicians
rationale: The core work is intensely physical: climbing 200-foot towers, rappelling to repair blades, lifting heavy parts, and hands-on mechanical/electrical repair in confined spaces—tasks AI cannot perform and only minimally assists via diagnostic monitoring. Elasticity is high because wind energy buildout is driven by surging electricity demand and clean energy policy, so cheaper/faster maintenance would enable more turbines to be deployed and serviced, with BLS projecting 50% employment growth. Despite strong demand growth, the disruption score is low because AI touches only the peripheral diagnostic and recordkeeping portions, leaving the physical core untouched, which places this firmly in the resilient category.

title: Woodworkers
rationale: Woodworking is predominantly physical and hands-on—cutting, shaping, sanding, assembling, finishing wood and handling heavy materials—with AI relevant only to peripheral tasks like blueprint interpretation or CNC programming. The disruption is driven by ongoing CNC automation rather than AI specifically, and core tasks still require human presence, dexterity, and judgment, so the disruption score stays low. Demand for wood products is structurally constrained by raw material costs, physical production limits, and consumer markets, with limited latent demand to unlock if production gets cheaper. Because disruption is well below the threshold, this occupation is resilient—AI touches the periphery but does not reshape the core manual work.

title: Writers and authors
rationale: Writing is almost entirely a digital, language-based task that sits squarely in the path of generative AI, which already produces drafts, copy, and content at scale — driving a very high disruption score. Demand is moderately elastic: cheaper content unlocks more marketing copy, blogs, and niche material, but prestige work (novels, screenplays, branded voice, original creative vision) and the sheer glut of low-value AI content cap how much human authorship total demand can absorb. Because disruption is very high (>=7) and elasticity is moderate (5), the occupation survives but shifts substantially toward editing, prompting, curation, and high-trust creative/voice work, displacing those who only produce commoditized prose.

title: Zoologists and wildlife biologists
rationale: The work splits between cognitive tasks (data analysis, GIS modeling, writing papers, population forecasting) where AI offers meaningful assistance, and irreducible physical fieldwork (collecting specimens, handling wildlife, observing animals in remote habitats) that requires human presence. AI accelerates the analytical and reporting portions but the core research still demands on-site data collection and expert judgment, placing disruption at a moderate 5. Demand is highly inelastic because employment is constrained by government and grant budgets rather than cost or speed of output—cheaper analysis won't dramatically expand the number of funded conservation positions. With disruption at or below 6, the occupation is resilient: AI touches the periphery and analytical tools without reshaping the fundamentally field-based, judgment-driven core.
